question: to the Commission Marieke Ehlers (PfE) Subject:

Following the judgment in Case C-769/22- Commission v Hungary1, the Court of Justice recognised that Article 2 of the Treaty on European Union (TEU) may function as a selfstanding legal basis in infringement proceedings under Article 258 Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. This development appears to strengthen the Commission’s capacity to address alleged breaches of EU values through judicial means, complementing the existing political mechanism under Article 7 TEU. 1.

How does the Commission intend to integrate Article 2 TEU as a stand-alone ground in its infringement strategy, and does it intend to prioritise Article 258 proceedings over initiating or advancing Article 7 TEU procedures?

To what extent does the Commission consider that judgments based directly on Article 2 TEU could serve as evidentiary or procedural support in ongoing or future Article 7 TEU proceedings against individual Member States?

How will the Commission ensure that the expanded use of Article 2 TEU in infringement actions respects the principle of conferral and avoids encroaching on Member States’ constitutional identities, without enforcing an ideological agenda on the individual Member States through lawfare?
ECLI:EU:C:2026:326.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (1.7.2026) The Commission has taken note of the landmark judgment of the Court of Justice in the infringement procedure launched by the Commission against Hungary in case C-769/221. In that judgment, the Court of Justice has found, for the first time, a separate infringement of Article 2 of the Treaty on the EU, which lists the values on which the EU is founded and which are common to all the Member States. The Commission, as guardian of the Treaties, will continue to use all the tools at its disposal to promote and uphold the values on which the EU is founded, in accordance with the case law of the Court of Justice. The infringement procedure, which is based on Article 258 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the EU and the procedure under Article 7 of the Treaty on the EU to which the Honourable Member refers, are separate procedures and rely on different mechanisms. There is no direct influence of the one over the other.
